sweep_bar.why: fix-boats (details pass, contacts): work_sweep with both hands on the sweep's crossbar. The kit stands the crew 0.15 m behind the bar (pt_sweep_crew, kit option sweep_crew_in) and puts the bar 0.85 m over their deck (sweep_bar_h): the take's palms are at 0.72-0.87 m (median), 0.1-0.5 m behind the bar line, and its hips rock 0.38 m fore and aft. Here the hips are held at z -0.08 (the feet kept where the take plants them) and both palms lie on the bar's line across the figure (y 0.85, z 0.15; bar radius 0.035 + the hand's half thickness 0.015). Shared by every sweep hand (boatman, inspector).

pole_hold_boatman.why: fix-boats: pole_boat with both hands on the pole and the pole still (boatman). The pole (props.json long_pole_low) is skinned to the hips, which the take turns and bends, so the pole swung through the deck under the man's feet while his palms were 0.14-0.36 m off it. Here the hips are frozen as the take has them at 0.9 s (turn and place; the feet kept), so the pole stays as it is then: slanting 65 deg, crossing the deck 0.58 m ahead of the root (the crew stand at the gunwale facing out: tools/crew_solve.mjs), its foot 2.5 m under the deck. Both palms lie on its axis (radius 0.04 + 0.015), sliding along it as the take pushes down. (Hold and freeze times differ by 0.5-1 ms: ik_clip poseAt at the same time twice in a row leaves the bones at rest, because three.js skips re-applying an unchanged value; reported to the lead.)

fend_up.why: fix-boats: fend_pole held still, raised 47 deg up to his right and a little ahead (the raised end 3.1 m high): pushing a pole up at an arch or a high stern (the take holds a raised pole in both hands only so; the figure is turned so it points at what it fends). The pole (long_pole_mid) is skinned to the right hand, which the take swings from overhead to waist height (the pole swept through the deck and the man) while the left palm was 0.34 m off it. Here the right hand is held in place and turn as the take has it at 3.8 s (frame Armature: still in the root frame), so the pole stays as it is then, and the left palm lies on its axis (radius 0.04 + 0.015). The figure is turned and placed so the forward end meets what it fends (tools/crew_solve.mjs, rule reach). The hips, spine and shoulders are frozen as at 3.8 s too, so the take's crouch (1.2-2.4 s, hands at 0.7 m) doesn't pull the hands off the still pole (the legs, neck and head keep the take's motion). (Hold and freeze times differ by 0.5-1 ms: ik_clip poseAt at the same time twice in a row leaves the bones at rest, because three.js skips re-applying an unchanged value; reported to the lead.)
